subject: VoyantHealth VPC packaging, scaling & platform-fee discount mechanics
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Sara Klein <sara.klein@voyanthealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-03T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: VoyantHealth VPC packaging, scale path and pilot SOW (updated)

Hi Sara,

Thanks again for the call earlier — good to map out the pilot goals. Attached is an updated starter SOW (Redwood_VPC_Starter-SOW-v2.docx) plus the commercial summary that aligns with the pilot scope we discussed (3 sites, operator licenses, observability addon).

A few items we highlighted:
- Platform fee (monthly) for pilot: $28k/mo (covers private control plane, support tier 2, telemetry retention)
- Operator licenses: 6 seats bundled for pilot duration
- Migration/implementation credit: we included a one-time $25k onboarding credit

Open points we wanted to confirm with you:
1) How you want to amortize the platform fee if you move to production (24 months vs 36 months)?
2) If usage grows beyond the pilot (GPU-hours or inference qps), we can shift to a scaled platform-fee discount — would you prefer a usage threshold (e.g., >1.2M tokens/day) or a committed capacity band?

Happy to walk through numbers tomorrow. If procurement wants an exportable commercial summary for their systems, let me know and I’ll include the HubSpot deal link and clean spreadsheet.

Thanks,
Jordan
Associate Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_VPC_Starter-SOW-v2.docx (docx), Voyant_DueDiligence_Security_Responses.pdf (pdf)

From: Sara Klein <sara.klein@voyanthealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@voyanthealth.com, Marcus Liu <marcus.liu@voyanthealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-04T11:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: VoyantHealth VPC packaging, scale path and pilot SOW (updated)

Jordan — thanks for the SOW and summary, appreciate the onboarding credit. A few quick clarifications from procurement/finance: 

- Platform fee amortization: finance prefers a 36-month amortization for capital planning, but leadership wants options for a 24-month ramp if we hit production KPIs earlier. Can Redwood provide pricing that shows both amortization scenarios?

- Scale discount mechanics: Voyant is sensitive to unit economics as we scale. We want a clear path where the platform fee steps down once we reach predictable usage — ideally tied to committed GPU-hours or a sustained qps floor rather than token estimates. Is Redwood open to a three-tier cadence (pilot / scale / enterprise) with defined trigger thresholds?

- Migration credits: the $25k credit is helpful; can some of that be conditional on accelerated delivery (e.g., drop-in if Redwood completes implementation within 6 weeks)?

Finally, legal asked for the security responses you attached — thanks. Marcus will coordinate any additional evidence.

Can Marissa or David weigh in on the three-tier idea and whether you can model a 36-month amortization in the commercial?

Best,
Sara
Head of Platform Programs
VoyantHealth

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-09-06T08:03:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: VoyantHealth VPC packaging, scale path and pilot SOW (updated) — pricing ask

Folks — forwarding Voyant’s procurement note (below). Key asks: show 36-mo amortization scenario, propose a three-tier platform-fee cadence tied to committed capacity (they prefer GPU-hours/qps triggers), and consider conditional onboarding credit for <6-week delivery.

Notes from the call: Voyant is likely to convert if unit economics work at ~1.5M tokens/day sustained or equivalent GPU-hour commitment. Finance wants conservative amortization.

Can we:
- Draft a quick commercial matrix with pilot / scale / enterprise rows showing platform fee $/mo and effective per-GPU-hour price (both 24 and 36-mo amortizations)
- Include a conditional onboarding credit variant (25k immediate vs 40k if delivery <=6 weeks)
- Confirm support tier definitions (SLA hours, on-call, response) — they asked explicitly about 24/7 vs business-hour on-call for the enterprise band

Happy to jump on a 30-min sync with Marissa and David — I can loop Voyant after.

— Jordan

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-08T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: VoyantHealth VPC packaging, scale path and pilot SOW (updated) — pricing ask

Thanks Jordan — below is a pragmatic construct we can send to Voyant. Numbers are illustrative and we should attach a short spreadsheet (will upload to the HubSpot deal). See OPS ticket OPS-789 for implementation assumptions.

Commercial construct (pilot -> enterprise):
- Pilot (months 0–3): Platform fee $28,000/mo; Operator bundle: 6 seats; Included 10TB telemetry retention; Support: Tier 2 (Business-hour on-call). One-time onboarding credit: $25,000.
- Scale (trigger: sustained >= 1.2M tokens/day OR committed 200 GPU-hrs/mo over 3 consecutive months): Platform fee steps to $18,000/mo (effective ~35% reduction); Support: Tier 3 (24/7 on-call for P1, 4-hr response). Migration credit option: $40,000 if delivery <=6 weeks (otherwise $25,000).
- Enterprise (trigger: sustained >= 3.0M tokens/day OR committed 800 GPU-hrs/mo): Platform fee steps to $12,000/mo; Support: Tier 3 + Quarterly SRE reviews and 24/7 escalation path; Volume rebate: negotiated annually based on committed node count.

Other items:
- Amortization scenarios: provide two columns in the sheet (24-mo vs 36-mo) for the platform fee impact on annual operating/capex planning. We can show per-GPU-hour equivalent and per-1M-tokens unit cost.
- SOW: David, can you confirm the SLA language for Tier 3 (hours, on-call rotations, severity definitions)? I recommend explicit P1 response SLAs and a credit matrix.
- Legal: require a 60-day rollback window on tier triggers to avoid unwarranted step-downs during bursty testing.

If this looks good I’ll draft an email back to Sara + procurement with the attached matrix and a redline SOW (minor edits to delivery milestones). Jordan, can you confirm whether Voyant needs a populated DocuSign packet or just redlines first?

— Marissa
Director, Commercial Offers
Redwood Inference

Related: HubSpot deal VOY-2026-VPC-01; Jira OPS-789

From: Sara Klein <sara.klein@voyanthealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@voyanthealth.com, Marcus Liu <marcus.liu@voyanthealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-10T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: VoyantHealth VPC packaging, scale path and pilot SOW (updated) — next steps

Marissa/Jordan — this is very helpful, thanks. Voyant is comfortable with the tier triggers you proposed (we prefer the GPU-hour trigger but the token proxy is fine for initial modeling). A couple of outstanding asks before we loop legal: 

1) Please return an updated commercial matrix with both amortization columns and a short worked example showing how the platform fee moves at the 1.2M token threshold (example month-by-month).
2) Add the conditional onboarding credit language to the SOW ("$40k if deployment completes within 6 weeks from contract signature; otherwise $25k").
3) We’d like a PoC clause in the SOW: 45-day pilot acceptance criteria and a clear go/no-go decision point tied to API latency and cost-per-token KPIs.

If we get that by EOD Monday our procurement/legal team will circulate redlines and a DocuSign-ready contract. Marcus will collect final security artifacts but the PDF you shared looked fine.

Agree in principle — excited to move to pilot.

Best,
Sara
Head of Platform Programs
VoyantHealth
